sanskrit: bharate bruvati svapnaṃ dūtās te klāntavāhanāḥ praviśyāsahyaparikhaṃ ramyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ puram
english: While Bharata was recounting his dream, those messengers with their weary horses entered the fair city of Rājagṛha, whose moat none could easily cross.

sanskrit: samāgamya tu rājñā ca rājaputreṇa cārcitāḥ rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tam ūcur bharataṃ vacaḥ
english: Having been received and honoured by both the king and the prince, they clasped the king's feet and then addressed these words to Bharata.

sanskrit: purohitas tvā kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ tvaramāṇaś ca niryāhi kṛtyam ātyayikaṃ tvayā
english: "The royal priest sends you his well-wishes, as do all the ministers. Depart with all speed — there is urgent business requiring your attention."

sanskrit: atra viṃśatikoṭyas tu nṛpater mātulasya te daśakoṭyas tu saṃpūrṇās tathaiva ca nṛpātmaja
english: "Here your maternal uncle the king offers twenty crores of gold, and ten crores fully complete besides, O son of a king."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvaṃ svanuraktaḥ suhṛjjane dūtān uvāca bharataḥ kāmaiḥ saṃpratipūjya tān
english: Bharata, ever affectionate toward his friends, accepted all those gifts, honoured the messengers with further presents, and then spoke to them.

sanskrit: kaccit sukuśalī rājā pitā daśaratho mama kaccic cārāgatā rāme lakṣmaṇe vā mahātmani
english: "Is my father King Daśaratha in good health? And is all well with great-souled Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa?"

sanskrit: āryā ca dharmaniratā dharmajñā dharmadarśinī arogā cāpi kausalyā mātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: "Is Kausalyā, the noble one devoted to righteousness, who knows and perceives dharma, mother of wise Rāma — is she free of illness?"

sanskrit: kaccit sumitrā dharmajñā jananī lakṣmaṇasya yā śatrughnasya ca vīrasya sārogā cāpi madhyamā
english: "Is Sumitrā, the dharma-knowing mother of Lakṣmaṇa and valiant Śatrughna — is that middle queen also free from illness?"

sanskrit: ātmakāmā sadā caṇḍī krodhanā prājñamāninī arogā cāpi kaikeyī mātā me kim uvāca ha
english: "And Kaikeyī — selfish, ever fierce, quick to anger, who thinks herself wise — is she too without illness? What has my mother been saying?"

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te dūtā bharatena mahātmanā ūcuḥ saṃpraśritaṃ vākyam idaṃ taṃ bharataṃ tadā kuśalās te naravyāghra yeṣāṃ kuśalam icchasi
english: When thus questioned by great-souled Bharata, the messengers gave this modest reply to him then: "Those whose welfare you seek are well, O tiger among men."

sanskrit: bharataś cāpi tān dūtān evam ukto 'bhyabhāṣata āpṛcche 'haṃ mahārājaṃ dūtāḥ saṃtvarayanti mām
english: Bharata, having heard their reply, in turn addressed the messengers: "I shall take leave of the great king; the messengers are urging me to make haste."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu tān dūtān bharataḥ pārthivātmajaḥ dūtaiḥ saṃcodito vākyaṃ mātāmaham uvāca ha
english: Having said this to the messengers, and being urged onward by them, Bharata the son of a king spoke these words to his maternal grandfather.

sanskrit: rājan pitur gamiṣyāmi sakāśaṃ dūtacoditaḥ punar apy aham eṣyāmi yadā me tvaṃ smariṣyasi
english: "O king, I shall go to my father, summoned as I am by the messengers. I will come again whenever you think of me."

sanskrit: bharatenaivam uktas tu nṛpo mātāmahas tadā tam uvāca śubhaṃ vākyaṃ śirasy āghrāya rāghavam
english: So addressed by Bharata, the king who was his maternal grandfather then smelled the Rāghava's head and spoke these auspicious words to him.

sanskrit: gaccha tātānujāne tvāṃ kaikeyī suprajās tvayā mātaraṃ kuśalaṃ brūyāḥ pitaraṃ ca paraṃtapa
english: "Go, my dear child, I permit you. Kaikeyī is blessed with such a son as you. Give my kind regards to your mother and father, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: purohitaṃ ca kuśalaṃ ye cānye dvijasattamāḥ tau ca tāta maheṣvāsau bhrātaru rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "And give my regards to the royal priest and to the other finest among the twice-born, and to those two great archers, your brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tasmai hastyuttamāṃś citrān kambalān ajināni ca abhisatkṛtya kaikeyo bharatāya dhanaṃ dadau
english: Honouring him fittingly, Kaikeya gave to Bharata fine elephant-loads of gifts — richly coloured woollen blankets and antelope skins.

sanskrit: rukma niṣkasahasre dve ṣoḍaśāśvaśatāni ca satkṛtya kaikeyī putraṃ kekayo dhanam ādiśat
english: Kekaya, honouring the son of Kaikeyī, bestowed wealth upon him: two thousand gold niṣkas and sixteen hundred horses.

sanskrit: tathāmātyān abhipretān viśvāsyāṃś ca guṇānvitān dadāv aśvapatiḥ śīghraṃ bharatāyānuyāyinaḥ
english: Aśvapati likewise promptly gave Bharata trustworthy, virtuous ministers of the kind he desired as companions for the journey.

sanskrit: airāvatān aindraśirān nāgān vai priyadarśanān kharāñ śīghrān susaṃyuktān mātulo 'smai dhanaṃ dadau
english: His maternal uncle gave him wealth in the form of fair-looking elephants of the Airāvata and Aindraśiras breeds, and swift, well-harnessed mules.

sanskrit: antaḥpure 'tisaṃvṛddhān vyāghravīryabalānvitān daṃṣṭrāyudhān mahākāyāñ śunaś copāyanaṃ dadau
english: He also presented as a gift hounds from the inner palace — great-bodied, armed with fangs, possessing the strength and ferocity of tigers.

sanskrit: sa mātāmaham āpṛcchya mātulaṃ ca yudhājitam ratham āruhya bharataḥ śatrughnasahito yayau
english: Taking leave of his maternal grandfather and his maternal uncle Yudhājit, Bharata mounted his chariot and departed, accompanied by Śatrughna.

sanskrit: rathān maṇḍalacakrāṃś ca yojayitvā paraḥśatam uṣṭrago'śvakharair bhṛtyā bharataṃ yāntam anvayuḥ
english: Having yoked more than a hundred chariots with circular wheels, the servants followed Bharata as he travelled, with camels, cattle, horses and mules.

sanskrit: balena gupto bharato mahātmā sahāryakasyātmasamair amātyaiḥ ādāya śatrughnam apetaśatrur gṛhād yayau siddha ivendralokāt
english: Great-souled Bharata, guarded by his army and accompanied by ministers as dear to him as kinsmen, took Śatrughna and departed from that house, like a perfected sage departing from the world of Indra.

sanskrit: sa prāṅmukho rājagṛhād abhiniryāya vīryavān hrādinīṃ dūrapārāṃ ca pratyaksrotas taraṅgiṇīm śatadrūṃ atarac chrīmān nadīm ikṣvākunandanaḥ
english: That valiant delight of the Ikṣvāku line, facing eastward, set forth from Rājagṛha and crossed the Śatadrū, that wide-banked, wave-bearing river flowing against the current, and the Hrādinī as well.

sanskrit: eladhāne nadīṃ tīrtvā prāpya cāparaparpaṭān śilām ākurvatīṃ tīrtvā āgneyaṃ śalyakartanam
english: Having crossed the river at Eladhāna and reached the Aparaparpaṭas, he crossed the rocky Śilā river and passed through Āgneya, the thorn-cutting region.

sanskrit: satyasaṃdhaḥ śuciḥ śrīmān prekṣamāṇaḥ śilāvahām atyayāt sa mahāśailān vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ prati
english: True to his pledges, pure, and splendid, he surveyed the stone-bearing river as he crossed the great mountains, making his way toward the Caitraratha forest.

sanskrit: veginīṃ ca kuliṅgākhyāṃ hrādinīṃ parvatāvṛtām yamunāṃ prāpya saṃtīrṇo balam āśvāsayat tadā
english: Crossing the swift river named Kuliṅgā and the Hrādinī girt by mountains, he reached the Yamunā and, having forded it, rested his troops.

sanskrit: śītīkṛtya tu gātrāṇi klāntān āśvāsya vājinaḥ tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca prāyād ādāya codakam
english: Having cooled his limbs, refreshed the weary horses, bathed and drunk there, he set off again, taking water along.

sanskrit: rājaputro mahāraṇyam anabhīkṣṇopasevitam bhadro bhadreṇa yānena mārutaḥ kham ivātyayāt
english: The auspicious prince, in his fine conveyance, crossed the great forest rarely traversed by others as swiftly as the wind crosses the sky.

sanskrit: toraṇaṃ dakṣiṇārdhena jambūprastham upāgamat varūthaṃ ca yayau ramyaṃ grāmaṃ daśarathātmajaḥ
english: Passing Toraṇa by its southern side, the son of Daśaratha reached Jambūprastha and then proceeded to the pleasant village of Varūtha.

sanskrit: tatra ramye vane vāsaṃ kṛtvāsau prāṅmukho yayau udyānam ujjihānāyāḥ priyakā yatra pādapāḥ
english: Having rested there in that lovely forest, he set off again facing eastward, toward the garden of Ujjihānā where the priyaka trees grow.

sanskrit: sālāṃs tu priyakān prāpya śīghrān āsthāya vājinaḥ anujñāpyātha bharato vāhinīṃ tvarito yayau
english: Reaching the sāla and priyaka groves, Bharata mounted swift horses, gave orders to the army, and pressed forward in haste.

sanskrit: vāsaṃ kṛtvā sarvatīrthe tīrtvā cottānakāṃ nadīm anyā nadīś ca vividhāḥ pārvatīyais turaṃgamaiḥ
english: Having rested at Sarvatīrtha and crossed the river Uttānakā and various other rivers with mountain-bred horses,

sanskrit: hastipṛṣṭhakam āsādya kuṭikām atyavartata tatāra ca naravyāghro lauhitye sa kapīvatīm ekasāle sthāṇumatīṃ vinate gomatīṃ nadīm
english: reaching Hastipṛṣṭhaka and passing through Kuṭikā, that tiger among men crossed the Kapīvatī at Lauhitya, and then the Ekasāla, Sthāṇumatī, and the river Gomatī at Vīṇatā.

sanskrit: kaliṅga nagare cāpi prāpya sālavanaṃ tadā bharataḥ kṣipram āgacchat supariśrāntavāhanaḥ
english: Then reaching the sāla forest near the city of Kaliṅga, Bharata arrived swiftly, though his horses were utterly exhausted.

sanskrit: vanaṃ ca samatītyāśu śarvaryām aruṇodaye ayodhyāṃ manunā rājñā nirmitāṃ sa dadarśa ha
english: Quickly crossing through the forest, at the crimson dawn following the dark of night, he caught sight of Ayodhyā, that city built by King Manu.

sanskrit: tāṃ purīṃ puruṣavyāghraḥ saptarātroṣiṭaḥ pathi ayodhyām agrato dṛṣṭvā rathe sārathim abravīt
english: That tiger among men, having spent seven nights on the road, saw Ayodhyā ahead and spoke from his chariot to the charioteer.

sanskrit: eṣā nātipratītā me puṇyodyānā yaśasvinī ayodhyā dṛśyate dūrāt sārathe pāṇḍumṛttikā
english: "This famed Ayodhyā with its holy gardens, seen from afar, does not appear altogether familiar to me, O charioteer — its soil looks pale."

sanskrit: yajvabhir guṇasaṃpannair brāhmaṇair vedapāragaiḥ bhūyiṣṭham ṛddhair ākīrṇā rājarṣivarapālitā
english: "Guarded by the best of royal sages, it was once filled to abundance with virtuous sacrificing Brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas."

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāṃ purāśabdaḥ śrūyate tumulo mahān samantān naranārīṇāṃ tam adya na śṛṇomy aham
english: "In Ayodhyā there always used to be heard a great tumultuous sound from men and women on all sides — today I do not hear it."

sanskrit: udyānāni hi sāyāhne krīḍitvoparatair naraiḥ samantād vipradhāvadbhiḥ prakāśante mamānyadā
english: "In the evenings the gardens used to shine on all sides with men who had finished their play and were hurrying about in every direction — but not so today."

sanskrit: tāny adyānurudantīva parityaktāni kāmibhiḥ araṇyabhūteva purī sārathe pratibhāti me
english: "Those gardens today seem to be weeping, as if abandoned by those who love pleasure. The city appears to me, O charioteer, as though it has become a wilderness."

sanskrit: na hy atra yānair dṛśyante na gajair na ca vājibhiḥ niryānto vābhiyānto vā naramukhyā yathāpuram
english: "Nor are the foremost men seen here coming and going as before, in their vehicles, on their elephants, or on their horses."

sanskrit: aniṣṭāni ca pāpāni paśyāmi vividhāni ca nimittāny amanojñāni tena sīdati te manaḥ
english: "I see various evil and sinister omens — unpleasant portents — and on account of these my heart is sinking."

sanskrit: dvāreṇa vaijayantena prāviśac chrāntavāhanaḥ dvāḥsthair utthāya vijayaṃ pṛṣṭas taiḥ sahito yayau
english: He entered through the Vaijayanta gate, his horses worn out. The gatekeepers rose to greet him and, after being asked for the welfare of those at the gate, accompanied him onward.

sanskrit: sa tv anekāgrahṛdayo dvāḥsthaṃ pratyarcya taṃ janam sūtam aśvapateḥ klāntam abravīt tatra rāghavaḥ
english: With his heart troubled by many forebodings, the Rāghava received the gatekeeper's people with honour and then spoke to the weary charioteer of Aśvapati.

sanskrit: śrutā no yādṛśāḥ pūrvaṃ nṛpatīnāṃ vināśane ākārās tān ahaṃ sarvān iha paśyāmi sārathe
english: "The signs I have heard of that betoken the ruin of kings — all of those signs I now see here, O charioteer."

sanskrit: malinaṃ cāśrupūrṇākṣaṃ dīnaṃ dhyānaparaṃ kṛśam sastrī puṃsaṃ ca paśyāmi janam utkaṇṭhitaṃ pure
english: "I see people in the city — both women and men — filthy, eyes brimming with tears, wretched, sunk in thought, emaciated, and long-suffering."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā bharataḥ sūtaṃ taṃ dīnamānasaḥ tāny aniṣṭāny ayodhyāyāṃ prekṣya rājagṛhaṃ yayau
english: Having spoken thus to the charioteer, Bharata with dejected heart, observing those ill omens in Ayodhyā, proceeded to the royal palace.

sanskrit: tāṃ śūnyaśṛṅgāṭakaveśmarathyāṃ rajo'ruṇadvārakapāṭayantrām dṛṣṭvā purīm indrapurī prakāśāṃ duḥkhena saṃpūrṇataro babhūva
english: Beholding that city — whose crossroads, houses, and streets were empty, whose gate-panels and bolts were reddened with dust — a city that once rivalled Indra's own in splendour — he became filled to overflowing with grief.

sanskrit: bahūni paśyan manaso 'priyāṇi yāny annyadā nāsya pure babhūvuḥ avākśirā dīnamanā nahṛṣṭaḥ pitur mahātmā praviveśa veśma
english: Seeing the many things unpleasant to his mind that had never existed before in his city, that great-souled man entered his father's palace with downcast head, dejected in mind, and devoid of joy.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃs tu tatas tatra pitaraṃ pitur ālaye jagāma bharato draṣṭuṃ mātaraṃ mātur ālaye
english: Not finding his father there in his father's dwelling, Bharata went to his mother's apartments to see his mother.

sanskrit: anuprāptaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā kaikeyī proṣitaṃ sutam utpapāta tadā hṛṣṭā tyaktvā sauvarṇamānasaṃ
english: When Kaikeyī saw her son who had returned from abroad, she sprang up with joy, leaving behind her golden seat.

sanskrit: sa praviśyaiva dharmātmā svagṛhaṃ śrīvivarjitam bharataḥ prekṣya jagrāha jananyāś caraṇau śubhau
english: Upon entering his own house and seeing it bereft of prosperity, the righteous-souled Bharata grasped the auspicious feet of his mother.

sanskrit: taṃ mūrdhni samupāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinam aṅke bharatam āropya praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Smelling his head in affectionate greeting, embracing that illustrious one, she seated Bharata on her lap and began to question him.

sanskrit: adya te kati cid rātryaś cyutasyāryakaveśmanaḥ api nādhvaśramaḥ śīghraṃ rathenāpatatas tava
english: "How many nights has it been now since you left your grandfather's house? Surely you have road-fatigue from coming so swiftly by chariot?"

sanskrit: āryakas te sukuśalo yudhājin mātulas tava pravāsāc ca sukhaṃ putra sarvaṃ me vaktum arhasi
english: "Is your grandfather in good health? And Yudhājit, your maternal uncle? Please tell me all, my son — was the sojourn pleasant in every respect?"

sanskrit: evaṃ pṛṣṭhas tu kaikeyyā priyaṃ pārthivanandanaḥ ācaṣṭa bharataḥ sarvaṃ mātre rājīvalocanaḥ
english: When thus questioned by Kaikeyī, lotus-eyed Bharata, delight of kings, told his mother everything she desired to know.

sanskrit: adya me saptamī rātriś cyutasyāryakaveśmanaḥ ambāyāḥ kuśalī tāto yudhājin mātulaś ca me
english: "This is the seventh night since I left my grandfather's house. My grandfather is well, O mother, and so is my uncle Yudhājit."

sanskrit: yan me dhanaṃ ca ratnaṃ ca dadau rājā paraṃtapaḥ pariśrāntaṃ pathy abhavat tato 'haṃ pūrvam āgataḥ
english: "The wealth and jewels that the mighty king gave me became exhausted on the road, and so I came on ahead of the rest."

sanskrit: rājavākyaharair dūtais tvaryamāṇo 'ham āgataḥ yad ahaṃ praṣṭum icchāmi tad ambā vaktum arhasi
english: "I came hastened by the messengers bearing the king's words. What I now wish to ask, O mother, you must tell me."

sanskrit: śūnyo 'yaṃ śayanīyas te paryaṅko hemabhūṣitaḥ na cāyam ikṣvākujanaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratibhāti me
english: "This gold-adorned couch of yours lies empty, and the people of the Ikṣvāku line do not appear joyful to me."

sanskrit: rājā bhavati bhūyiṣṭham ihāmbāyā niveśane tam ahaṃ nādya paśyāmi draṣṭum icchann ihāgataḥ
english: "The king is generally to be found here in your apartments, O mother. I do not see him today, though I have come here wishing to see him."

sanskrit: pitur grahīṣye caraṇau taṃ mamākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ āhosvid amba jyeṣṭhāyāḥ kausalyāyā niveśane
english: "I want to clasp my father's feet — tell me where he is, I ask you. Is he perhaps in the apartments of the eldest, Kausalyā?"

sanskrit: taṃ pratyuvāca kaikeyī priyavad ghoram apriyam ajānantaṃ prajānantī rājyalobhena mohitā yā gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ te pitā gataḥ
english: Kaikeyī answered him with words that were dreadful though spoken tenderly — she who should have known better yet was blinded by greed for the kingdom, addressing him as though he did not know: "The end that comes to all living beings — your father has gone to that end."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bharato vākyaṃ dharmābhijanavāñ śuciḥ papāta sahasā bhūmau pitṛśokabalārditaḥ
english: Hearing those words, Bharata — pure, of noble lineage, devoted to righteousness — suddenly fell to the ground, overwhelmed by the force of grief for his father.

sanskrit: tataḥ śokena saṃvītaḥ pitur maraṇaduḥkhitaḥ vilalāpa mahātejā bhrāntākulitacetanaḥ
english: Then, enveloped in grief, tormented by the pain of his father's death, that great and illustrious one lamented, his mind distraught and agitated.

sanskrit: etat suruciraṃ bhāti pitur me śayanaṃ purā tad idaṃ na vibhāty adya vihīnaṃ tena dhīmatā
english: "This was once the very beautiful couch of my father — today it does not shine, bereft as it is of that wise one."

sanskrit: tam ārtaṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ samīkṣya patitaṃ bhuvi utthāpayitvā śokārtaṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Beholding him thus afflicted and fallen to the ground — he who was like a god — she raised up the grief-stricken one and spoke these words.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kiṃ śeṣe rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ tvadvidhā na hi śocanti santaḥ sadasi saṃmatāḥ
english: "Rise up, rise up — why do you lie prostrate, O prince of great renown? Men of your kind do not grieve — the righteous who are honoured in assemblies do not."

sanskrit: sa rudatyā ciraṃ kālaṃ bhūmau viparivṛtya ca jananīṃ pratyuvācedaṃ śokair bahubhir āvṛtaḥ
english: He, having wept for a long time and rolled on the ground, then spoke these words to his mother, wrapped in manifold griefs.

sanskrit: abhiṣekṣyati rāmaṃ tu rājā yajñaṃ nu yakṣyati ity ahaṃ kṛtasaṃkalpo hṛṣṭo yātrām ayāsiṣam
english: "'The king will consecrate Rāma; he will perform the sacrifice' — with this resolve and in gladness I set out on the journey."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ hy anyathā bhūtaṃ vyavadīrṇaṃ mano mama pitaraṃ yo na paśyāmi nityaṃ priyahite ratam
english: "But all of this has turned out otherwise, and my mind is split with anguish, for I do not see my father, who was ever devoted to what was dear and beneficial."

sanskrit: amba kenātyagād rājā vyādhinā mayy anāgate dhanyā rāmādayaḥ sarve yaiḥ pitā saṃskṛtaḥ svayam
english: "By what illness did the king pass away in my absence, O mother? Blessed are all of them — Rāma and the others — by whom the last rites of our father were themselves performed."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ māṃ mahārājaḥ prāptaṃ jānāti kīrtimān upajighred dhi māṃ mūrdhni tātaḥ saṃnamya satvaram
english: "Surely the illustrious great king does not know that I have arrived — for otherwise my father would have hastened to bend down and smell my head in greeting."

sanskrit: kva sa pāṇiḥ sukhasparśas tātasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ yena māṃ rajasā dhvastam abhīkṣṇaṃ parimārjati
english: "Where is that gentle hand of my father of blameless deeds, with which he used to wipe the dust from me time and again?"

sanskrit: yo me bhrātā pitā bandhur yasya dāso 'smi dhīmataḥ tasya māṃ śīghram ākhyāhi rāmasyākliṣṭa karmaṇaḥ
english: "He who is my brother, my father, and my kinsman — of that wise Rāma of blameless deeds whose servant I am — tell me of him quickly."

sanskrit: pitā hi bhavati jyeṣṭho dharmam āryasya jānataḥ tasya pādau grahīṣyāmi sa hīdānīṃ gatir mama
english: "For the eldest son who knows dharma becomes a father to the noble man. I will grasp his feet — he is my refuge now."

sanskrit: ārye kim abravīd rājā pitā me satyavikramaḥ paścimaṃ sādhu saṃdeśam icchāmi śrotum ātmanaḥ
english: "What did the king, my father of true valour, say at the last, O noble lady? I wish to hear his final good message for me."

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭā yathātattvaṃ kaikeyī vākyam abravīt rāmeti rājā vilapan hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca sa mahātmā paraṃ lokaṃ gato gatimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Thus asked truthfully, Kaikeyī spoke: "Lamenting 'Rāma!', 'Ah, Sītā!', 'Lakṣmaṇa!', that great-souled one, the foremost among those who have attained the highest goal, departed to the other world."

sanskrit: imāṃ tu paścimāṃ vācaṃ vyājahāra pitā tava kāla dharmaparikṣiptaḥ pāśair iva mahāgajaḥ
english: "This was the last utterance of your father — seized by the noose of Time and Death's law, like a great elephant caught in a snare."

sanskrit: siddhārthās tu narā rāmam āgataṃ sītayā saha lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābāhuṃ drakṣyanti punar āgatam
english: "Those men will have achieved their purpose who will see Rāma return together with Sītā and long-armed Lakṣmaṇa come back again."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā viṣasādaiva dvitīyā priyaśaṃsanāt viṣaṇṇavadano bhūtvā bhūyaḥ papraccha mātaram
english: Hearing this second piece of dear news yet sinking still further, his face despondent, he questioned his mother again.

sanskrit: kva cedānīṃ sa dharmātmā kausalyānandavardhanaḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca samaṃ gataḥ
english: "Where has that righteous soul gone now — he who is the increaser of Kausalyā's joy — together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā?"

sanskrit: tathā pṛṣṭā yathātattvam ākhyātum upacakrame mātāsya yugapad vākyaṃ vipriyaṃ priyaśaṅkayā
english: Thus asked, his mother proceeded to tell the full truth, delivering an unwelcome word in the hope that it would be taken as welcome.

sanskrit: sa hi rājasutaḥ putra cīravāsā mahāvanam daṇḍakān saha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇānucaro gataḥ
english: "For that prince, my son, clad in bark-garments, has gone to the great Daṇḍaka forest together with the daughter of Videha, followed by Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bharatas trasto bhrātuś cāritraśaṅkayā svasya vaṃśasya māhātmyāt praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Hearing this, Bharata was alarmed and, out of anxiety regarding his brother's conduct and the greatness of his own lineage, proceeded to enquire further.

sanskrit: kaccin na brāhmaṇavadhaṃ hṛtaṃ rāmeṇa kasya cit kaccin nāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ
english: "Has Rāma taken the life of any Brāhmaṇa? Has he caused harm to any innocent person — rich or poor?"

sanskrit: kaccin na paradārān vā rājaputro 'bhimanyate kasmāt sa daṇḍakāraṇye bhrūṇaheva vivāsitaḥ
english: "Or does the prince lust after another man's wife? Why has he been banished to the Daṇḍaka forest like one who has slain an embryo?"

sanskrit: athāsya capalā mātā tat svakarma yathātatham tenaiva strīsvabhāvena vyāhartum upacakrame
english: Then his fickle mother, in keeping with her own nature as a woman, began to speak of her own deed exactly as it had occurred.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇadhanaṃ kiṃ cid dhṛtaṃ rāmeṇa kasya cit kaś cin nāḍhyo daridro vā tenāpāpo vihiṃsitaḥ na rāmaḥ paradārāṃś ca cakṣurbhyām api paśyati
english: "Rāma has taken no property of any Brāhmaṇa; he has harmed no innocent person, rich or poor; nor does Rāma even glance with his eyes at another man's wife."

sanskrit: mayā tu putra śrutvaiva rāmasyaivābhiṣecanam yācitas te pitā rājyaṃ rāmasya ca vivāsanam
english: "But I, my son, as soon as I heard of Rāma's consecration, asked your father for the kingdom and for Rāma's banishment."

sanskrit: sa svavṛttiṃ samāsthāya pitā te tat tathākarot rāmaś ca sahasaumitriḥ preṣitaḥ saha sītayā
english: "Your father, abiding by his own nature, did exactly that; and Rāma was sent away along with Saumitri and Sītā."

sanskrit: tam apaśyan priyaṃ putraṃ mahīpālo mahāyaśāḥ putraśokaparidyūnaḥ pañcatvam upapedivān
english: "That ruler of the earth of great renown, not beholding his beloved son, consumed by grief over his son, attained the five elements — that is, he died."

sanskrit: tvayā tv idānīṃ dharmajña rājatvam avalambyatām tvatkṛte hi mayā sarvam idam evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtam
english: "Now, O knower of dharma, the kingship must be taken up by you — for it was for your sake that I did all of this."

sanskrit: tat putra śīghraṃ vidhinā vidhijñair vasiṣṭhamukhyaiḥ sahito dvijendraiḥ saṃkālya rājānam adīnasattvam ātmānam urvyām abhiṣecayasva
english: "Therefore, my son, quickly, in accordance with rite, together with Vasiṣṭha at the head of the brahmins who know the ritual — summon the king and have yourself, a man of undaunted spirit, consecrated on this earth."
